overview: Based on the published agenda, the D.C. Everest Area School District Board of Education was scheduled to hold a regular meeting on July 15, 2026, to address staffing changes, policy updates, budget matters, and curriculum reviews. The agenda included multiple second readings of policy revisions, approval of school handbooks for the 2026-27 school year, and presentations on facilities planning and student screen time, along with routine financial and employment consent items.

discussions.body: Shannon Grabko was scheduled to present information regarding the WASB Legislative Network and its relevance to the district.
Larry Schaefer was scheduled to present as the CESA #9 representative, providing regional cooperative educational services information to the board.

Dr. Casey Nye was scheduled to present multiple reports including a district update, certified staff compensation planning, internal review of student screen time, facilities study learning focus, information on Responsive Classroom initiatives, summer projects update, and information on the 2026 World Horseshoe Pitching Championship being hosted by the district.

discussions.item: Set the Date for Annual Meeting/Budget Hearing
discussions.body: The board was expected to establish the date for the district's annual meeting and budget hearing for the upcoming fiscal year.
The board was scheduled to review and consider academic standards for the 2026-27 school year.
The board was expected to approve a list of independent hearing officers for the district.
The board was scheduled to review handbooks from all school levels including elementary (Riverside sample), middle school, junior high, and senior high for the 2026-27 school year.

discussions.item: Review of po2261.01 - Parent and Family Engagement in Title 1 Programs
discussions.body: The board was expected to review and consider the Parent and Family Engagement in Title 1 Programs policy.
The Reading Specialist was scheduled to present an annual report evaluating the district's reading curriculum, including kindergarten assessment updates and reading instructional goals for July 2026.
The board was expected to consider approval for a senior high trip to Japan.

The board was scheduled to conduct first readings of nine policies addressing student supervision and welfare, job descriptions, personal communication devices, student technology acceptable use and safety, social media use, and volunteers and abuse reporting procedures.
